6.stimulus: A trend away from stable, relatively high humidity in the Middle East over the past 8 million years can be inferred from the composition of cave formations dating to different periods. Cave formations from about 7 million years ago mainly consist of transparent columnar calcite, indicative of an underground water system regularly replenished by rainfall. Cave formations younger than approximately 1 million years, however, mainly consist of branching, opaque (and sometimes colorful) material, often with more frequent growth interruptions, indicating an intermittent water supply.
6.text: Which choice best describes the function of the two underlined portions in the text as a whole?

choices.A: They identify different characteristics of cave formations that when considered together provide evidence for a long-term shift toward lower and more variable humidity in the Middle East.
choices.B: They describe divergent features of cave formations that when taken together imply decreasing variation in Middle Eastern rainfall over time.
choices.C: They draw a contrast between Middle Eastern cave formations that is suggestive of geographic differences in the underground water supply.
choices.D: They provide evidence from different Middle Eastern cave formations that substantiates the claim that the region has experienced a consistent increase in total annual rainfall over the same period.

7.stimulus: In many parts of the world, merchants rarely label goods with exact prices like $17.31 or $203.62. Studies have shown that consumers view exact prices as reflecting merchant expertise and careful calculation, so why aren't they more common? One reason is that exact prices may create greater cognitive friction during purchase decisions than do whole-number prices or prices easily rounded to whole numbers (e.g., $5.99, which is little different from $6). Particularly if multiple goods are being considered for purchase, tracking and comparing exact prices may feel onerous to consumers.
7.text: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To account for the fact that exact prices remain uncommon in many places despite some positive consumer perceptions of them
choices.B: To argue that exact prices are relatively uncommon because calculating them is burdensome for merchants
choices.C: To address the question of why the use of exact prices is less common in some parts of the world than in others
choices.D: To explain why exact prices present greater cognitive friction for some consumers than whole-number prices or easily rounded prices do

8.stimulus:
Text 1
For decades, ornithologists assumed that if they saw a singing Bell's vireo—a bird species found in temperate North America—they must be observing a male. That's because birdsong has long been considered a male trait; researchers have argued that singing enables males to attract mates and claim territory.

Text 2
Recent evidence shows that a female Bell's vireo is as capable of song as a male is. In fact, Karan J. Odom and colleagues found evidence of female song in 71% of the 323 species they examined. They claim that the historical mischaracterization of birdsong as a male trait is largely the result of bias: much of the research ornithologists have carried out has been near universities in the temperate northern hemisphere, where female birdsong is less common than it is in the tropics.
8.text: Based on the texts, how would Odom and colleagues (Text 2) most likely respond to the view of birdsong presented in Text 1?

choices.A: They would suggest that it reflects a tendency to study male birds rather than female birds.
choices.B: They would claim that other factors than mate attraction and territorial defense have driven the evolution of singing in male birds.
choices.C: They would underscore that male songbirds in temperate zones are likely using their songs for different purposes than are male songbirds in the tropics.
choices.D: They would argue that it was influenced by the kinds of study sites researchers tended to select.

9.stimulus: Synthetic elements with very heavy nuclei, such as darmstadtium (Ds) and flerovium (Fl), can exhibit behaviors that make these elements challenging to classify. The earliest experiment with Fl revealed properties associated with noble gases, while a second experiment found that Fl acts like a volatile metal. When Yakushev, Lens, et al. studied interactions between Fl and gold surfaces, they found that Fl is less reactive than the volatile metal mercury but is more reactive than the noble gas radon. These results confirm that Fl forms chemical bonds with gold, but the mechanisms of these reactions are unclear.
9.text: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Observed inconsistencies in the behavior of Fl across experiments can be attributed to its interactions with other elements with very heavy nuclei.
choices.B: Although experiments have indicated that Fl is similar to the noble gases, it is too reactive to belong to this class of elements.
choices.C: Experiments have shown that properties of Fl do not precisely align with existing classifications of elements.
choices.D: Although Fl forms chemical bonds with gold surfaces in experiments, it does not react with volatile metals or noble gases.

10.stimulus: Thurgood Marshall saw litigation as a means to enact social reforms and advance equal justice for US citizens. He cited the law's "capacity to initiate change and its flexibility to accept and mold change" as vital, breaking with the historical tradition of wielding the courts primarily to clarify or modify existing laws. This vision was realized in Marshall's successful arguing of the 1954 Brown v. Board of Education case before the US Supreme Court, as the court's decision to overturn the long-standing "separate but equal" doctrine revolutionized how the legal system regarded civil rights.
10.text: Based on the text, how did Marshall's Brown v. Board of Education case most likely influence the US legal system's approach to civil rights?

choices.A: It promoted the idea that legal action is the most efficient way to create social change.
choices.B: It established that the courts could be used as a tool for significant social change.
choices.C: It inadvertently resulted in the courts taking a more cautious, incremental approach to advancing subsequent civil rights cases.
choices.D: It led courts to focus more on clarifying existing civil rights laws than on making modifications to them.

11.stimulus: While US public charities, such as Kaiser Foundation Hospitals, must file Form 990 yearly with the IRS, private foundations, such as the David and Lucile Packard Foundation, must file a different form, 990-PF. In addition, foundations that engage in certain prohibited activities must also file Form 4720 and pay penalty taxes on the money involved. Prohibited activities for private foundations include "self-dealing" (conducting activities that benefit foundation insiders), making taxable expenditures such as outlays for lobbying, and failing to cross a required threshold in making charitable distributions from income. Out of the organizations that filed Form 990-PF in 2005, ______
11.text: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the assertion?

choices.A: those that filed Form 4720 because they engaged in self-dealing and those that filed Form 4720 because of their taxable expenditures collectively paid a smaller portion of the total penalty than those that filed Form 4720 because they did not meet the minimum charitable distribution requirement.
choices.B: those that filed Form 4720 because they engaged in self-dealing paid, on average, lower penalties than those that filed Form 4720 because they did not meet the minimum charitable distribution requirement.
choices.C: more filed Form 4720 because they failed to meet the minimum charitable distribution requirement than did so in the following year.
choices.D: those that filed Form 4720 because they engaged in self-dealing and those that filed Form 4720 because of their taxable expenditures collectively accounted for a majority of the total penalties assessed.

12.stimulus: Mollusk shells are mainly composed of calcium carbonate, a chemical compound used in mortar and other construction materials. A research team led by Ariane da Silva Cardoso investigated pulverizing discarded Sururu mussel shells to create a substitute for fine aggregates (such as sand) in mortar mixtures. The team prepared mixtures with Sururu shell aggregate (SSA) replacing varying percentages of sand and then tested the mortars' compressive strength on days 7 and 28 of curing. Based on their findings, the team recommended SSA substitution in relatively small proportions to avoid compromising strength.
12.text: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support the researchers' recommendation?

choices.A: The compressive strength of the 10% SSA mixture never surpassed the compressive strength measured for the control mixture on day 28.
choices.B: The compressive strength of the 10% SSA mixture remained nearly the same from day 7 to day 28, while that of the 20% and 40% SSA mixtures changed substantially.
choices.C: The 10% SSA mixture's compressive strength was greater than or approximately equal to that of the control mixture on day 7 and on day 28, but on both days the 20% and 40% SSA mixtures had less compressive strength than the control mixture did.
choices.D: The 10% SSA mixture's compressive strength was greater than that of the control mixture on day 7, but by day 28 the 10% SSA mixture's compressive strength had decreased while that of the control mixture had increased.

13.stimulus: A student is writing a research paper on the history of irrigation in the state of California, situating the development of the Dodge Reservoir (created in Lassen County, California, in 1893) in a larger historical context. 13.text: Which quotation from a study of California agriculture best supports the student's claim?

choices.A: While the low humidity of Southern California's desert areas makes irrigation a requirement if agriculture is to be a success there, the relatively high humidity in the northern parts of the state makes such practices less necessary.
choices.B: The necessity of irrigation infrastructure in California today cannot be overstated, since it is the most common means of conveying water for agricultural use.
choices.C: The irrigation system developed by the Hohokam people in the 7th century CE in what is now Arizona was simple but applied hydraulic engineering design features that are still used today in both Arizona and California.
choices.D: Competition for scarce water resources in Southern California inspired the development of sprinkler irrigation systems, a manner of irrigating that requires less use of water than traditional surface irrigation methods.

14.stimulus: A 2025 study performed by Simon Townsend and colleagues presents evidence that bonobos, close relatives of chimpanzees, are capable of a rudimentary compositionality in communication—that is, they can organize sounds they make such that the order carries meaning in addition to the sounds themselves. After reviewing bonobo calls recorded in forests of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Townsend's team claimed that bonobos sometimes paired calls in specific orders and that the contexts of such pairs indicate they were deliberate communications rather than products of chance. The team based their claim on mathematical analysis of bonobo call sequences.
14.text: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' claim?

choices.A: A bonobo grunt seems to function as a request for other bonobos to join in whatever activity is ongoing, since bonobos emitting a grunt did so during potentially collaborative contexts such as feeding, nesting, and grooming.
choices.B: Bonobos used a single yelp or a single peep as an imperative, but a yelp appeared to be closer to a command, while a peep tended to function as a suggestion.
choices.C: While a single whistle from a bonobo was often an attempt to organize groups, a whistle preceded by a peep sound usually occurred in the presence of a charged social situation.
choices.D: When bonobos paired grunts with other calls, they did not necessarily adhere to a fixed sequence, and the communicative function of the calls did not shift.

15.stimulus: Here is an adaptation of established fiction genres to Southern contexts. Mark Twain derived his episodic narrative structures and roguish heroes from the picaresque novel, and William Faulkner realized the decadent aristocrat, the imperiled heroine, and other character types of the Gothic novel as rural Southerners who were more contingent, more caught in the net of societal relations and history than the fantastical figures of the Gothic had been. Some of the region's poets, such as James Dickey, have shown even greater dexterity by adapting these sources in an altogether different literary form.
15.text: Which statement, if true, would most directly support the underlined sentence?

choices.A: With its rural settings and rustic characters, Dickey's poems suggest the influence of the genre of pastoral fiction, yet Dickey may have instead obtained these elements from pastoral poetry, which preceded its namesake in fiction.
choices.B: The Gothic genre emerged in England and Ireland in the 1700s and was later naturalized to the cultural landscape of the Northeastern US, as in the novels of Nathaniel Hawthorne, which Dickey had almost certainly read.
choices.C: When Dickey invokes one genre of poetry and, within the space of a few lines, abandons it for another genre of poetry, what can we infer from this gesture if not the poet's fascination with genre per se, as well as his discomfort with it?
choices.D: "What is the disturbed, and disturbing, speaker of Dickey's best poems if not a stock character of the Gothic novel, refracted through the speech and ethos of the South and conditioned by the structures of lyric poetry?"

26.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ynés Mexía was a Mexican American botanist.
• Between 1917 and 1938, she collected over 150,000 botanical samples throughout the Americas.
• She collected a sample of Porophyllum ruderale in Minas Gerais, Brazil, in 1930.
• She collected a sample of Brickellia diffusa in Jalisco, Mexico, in 1926.
• Porophyllum ruderale and Brickellia diffusa are part of the Asteraceae family.
• These specimens can now be viewed online at the C.V. Starr Virtual Herbarium.
26.text: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to introduce Mexía to a new audience?

choices.A: Many of the botanical samples collected by Ynés Mexía, such as Porophyllum ruderale and Brickellia diffusa, can now be viewed on the C.V. Starr Virtual Herbarium.
choices.B: Botanist Ynés Mexía is known for collecting over 150,000 botanical samples throughout the Americas between 1917 and 1938.
choices.C: Among the many botanical samples Ynés Mexía collected in Brazil in 1930 was Porophyllum ruderale of the Asteraceae family.
choices.D: Between 1917 and 1938, Ynés Mexía collected samples of the plants Porophyllum ruderale and Brickellia diffusa, among many others, but her work was largely ignored by the scientific community during her lifetime.

27.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Marta Danielsdottir et al.'s 2007 study of planktonic ecosystems used a nutrient–phytoplankton–zooplankton (NPZ) model.
• Diane Stoecker et al. (2017): NPZ models rely "on the differentiation of the planktonic communities into phytoplankton or zooplankton functional types," excluding mixotrophic plankton.
• Phytoplankton are exclusively phototrophic, producing nutrients via photosynthesis.
• Zooplankton are exclusively phagotrophic, obtaining nutrients by consuming other organisms.
27.text: The student wants to challenge the model used in Danielsdottir et al.'s study. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Since it classifies plankton as exclusively phototrophic producers or phagotrophic consumers, the model used in Danielsdottir et al.'s study may misrepresent planktonic ecosystems, in which—as Stoecker et al. note—many plankton combine these functions.
choices.B: Danielsdottir et al.'s model disregards the respective roles of producers and consumers—organisms that, as Stoecker et al. emphasize, are essential to the trophic structure of the plankton food web.
choices.C: By restricting planktonic functional types to phytoplankton and zooplankton, the model used in Danielsdottir et al.'s study of planktonic ecosystems overlooks the many mixotrophic species that Stoecker et al. identify as being excluded from NPZ models.
choices.D: Stoecker et al. argue that the NPZ model used in the 2007 study by Danielsdottir et al. is a common tool for studying the differentiation of phytoplankton and zooplankton functional types in various ecosystems.
